sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Runtime packages
sections.what: Lists the packages the app needs while running, grouped by job: web framework, database, data handling, statistics, graph analysis, web research, validation, security, logging, export files, and utilities.
sections.why: Each group is labeled, which makes it easier to see what each package is for.
sections.watch_out: Versions are linked, so upgrading one package, such as pydantic, can break others that depend on it; Redis and Celery must be uncommented to use them.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Test and development tools
sections.what: Lists tools for running tests, checking code style, type checking, and pre-commit hooks. Also lists helpers for XML, currency rates, robots.txt rules, and rate limiting.
sections.why: Likely reason: the research and export code uses the helper packages, and the other tools support development. No further reason is stated.
sections.watch_out: These tools are installed everywhere this file is used, including any shared or production server, which adds packages to maintain.

summary: Lists the Python packages and exact versions the API needs, so the same setup can be installed on any machine.
purpose: Lets anyone install the same package versions the developers used.
why: Pinned versions keep results repeatable across machines. The reason for this exact list is not stated in the file.
how: 1. Each line names a package and a fixed version. 2. Lines are grouped by purpose with comments. 3. Installing with pip reads this file and installs every listed package, including test and development tools.
inputs: Read by pip during installation. Nothing reads it while the app runs.
outputs: An installed set of packages in the Python environment.
risks: Test and development tools are installed alongside runtime packages. Some packages are listed twice with the same version. Older pins may have known problems that were not checked here. Redis and Celery are commented out, though the environment file has settings for them.
debug: If installation fails, note which package and version failed, then check that the version works with your Python version, which is not stated here. If a package is missing at runtime, confirm it is listed and installed in the same environment the app runs in.
